claim: The romaji line for 時間 keeps the book's placeholder tilde ('~jikan') although the front, which drops the tilde as the pilot rule says, reads 時間 alone; the sister card 一時間 reads 'ichi-jikan' with no tilde.
evidence: Book, Vocabulary > Time: '〜じかん 〜時間 . . . hours'. cards.json r-09558b2cc685: target 時間, ttsText じかん, pronunciation '~jikan', english 'Time; ... hours (duration)'. r-0ce8b690e987 一時間: pronunciation 'ichi-jikan'.
verdictReason: Checked in cards.json: target 時間 and ttsText じかん carry no tilde (the merge strips the book's placeholder tilde from the reading, src/reading/readingPhase.js), but the romanization pass kept it (candidates/romanization.json 'r-09558b2cc685: ~jikan') and it renders as 'Says: ~jikan'. Both roles filed this under the same id, so one line. The Learner's second point, that the English should lose '... hours', is not taken: 'Time; ... hours' is the book's own gloss for the word (R&W 3 kanji table: 時間 'time; . . . hours'; Lesson 4 vocabulary: 〜時間 '. . . hours'), so only the romaji changes. The same defect exists in chapter-13 (a card with pronunciation '~dai'), outside this chapter.

claim: The English adds 'Health and' that nothing on the front supports, so a learner who reads the front correctly as 'Sports Day' marks themselves wrong.
evidence: Front: 'スポーツの日'. Back: 'Answer: Health and Sports Day / Says: supōtsu no hi'. Ledger: 'スポーツ | Sports'; chapter-4 card r-15917f3b3261 '日' = 'Day; sun'.
fix: Gloss it as 'Sports Day', or add a note that the English name still carries the older 'Health and Sports Day' wording.
verdictReason: Faithful to the book: the Culture Notes holiday table prints 'スポーツの 日 Health and Sports Day' (chapter 6, 日本の祝日), and a finding never says the book is wrong. A reading card has no note field for the suggested remark (docs/card-rules-reading.md: no scene, hint or note).

claim: The kanji is glossed only as 'Ahead', which points forward in time, while every 先 word in this chapter means 'last' or 'previous', so a learner reading 先月 or 先週 cold guesses 'next month' or 'next week'.
evidence: Front: '先'. Back: 'Answer: Ahead / Says: sen / saki'. Same unit: r-0eae6c9a0cef '先月' = 'Last month', r-66a936beb454 '先週' = 'Last week'.
fix: Gloss it as 'Ahead; previous' so the sense the chapter's words use is on the card.
verdictReason: The card carries the book's own gloss. Genki R&W 6 (chapter 20) kanji table: '先 (ahead) ▶せん ▷さき 先生 teacher, 先週 last week, 先に ahead, 先月 last month', and the card's reviewNote records that its data came from that table. Design 10-character-cards.md says the book's meaning replaces the generated one once the book teaches the kanji, and card-rules design rule 8 says a character's English is the meanings the book gives. Adding 'previous' would be editing the book's gloss.

claim: The reading kotoshi cannot be built from the readings the 今 and 年 cards taught, and the back does not say it is a whole-word reading, so a learner who reads it as konnen thinks they misremembered the kanji cards.
evidence: Front: '今年'. Back: 'Answer: This year / Says: kotoshi'. Kanji cards: chapter-4 '今' (kon, kin / ima) and this unit's r-6f14c2641c25 '年 ... Says: nen / toshi'. Compare 今週 'konshū' and 今月 'kongetsu' in this unit, which do follow the kanji readings.
fix: Mark the back as a special reading of the whole word, not built from the kanji's own readings.
verdictReason: Same ruling as chapter-4's 今日/明日 findings: the book prints ことし（今年） in the Useful Expressions time table and 今年(ことし) in the R&W 5 kanji table with no remark, the reading deck has no place for one (card-rules-reading.md forbids a note, hint or pronunciation field on a reading card; reviewNote is never rendered), and design 10-character-cards.md (owner, 2026-09-28) settles that a silent kanji card is graded on meaning alone with its readings as a reference, the word's reading being learned from the word card. A whole-word-reading marker would be a new design convention, not a card fix.

claim: The reading kinō cannot be built from the 昨 card's only reading, and the back does not say it is a whole-word reading, so a learner who reads it as sakujitsu thinks they misremembered the kanji card.
evidence: Front: '昨日'. Back: 'Answer: Yesterday / Says: kinō'. This unit's r-8f0005d18f7e '昨 ... Says: saku'.
fix: Mark the back as a special reading of the whole word, not built from the kanji's own readings.
verdictReason: Same ruling as 今年 and chapter-4's 今日: the book prints きのう 昨日 (Lesson 4 vocabulary) and きのう（昨日） (Useful Expressions) with no remark; the reading card has no note field to carry the marker; design 10-character-cards.md settles that the kanji card's readings are a reference and the word card teaches the word's reading. The 昨 card's single reading 'saku' is what KANJIDIC2 and the jōyō table give, so it is not wrong either.

claim: The vocabulary entry 時 (とき, 'when; at the time of') has no card: the build generated it, then dropped it as a repeat of chapter-4's silent kanji card 時, whose English is only 'Time', so the word's meaning and reading appear nowhere in the deck.
evidence: Book, Vocabulary > Time: 'とき 時 when . . . ; at the time of . . . (〜の)'. chapter-5/as-generated.json has {target 時, english 'When; at the time of', ttsText とき, id r-2fdc2b012a91}; chapter-5/cards.json has no 時, and reading-report.json lists no drop for it. chapter-4/cards.json r-2fdc2b012a91: target 時, english 'Time', pronunciation 'ji / toki', silent character card from the R&W 3 kanji table.
fix: Give the one 時 card (r-2fdc2b012a91) both senses, e.g. 'Time; when (at the time of)', or make it the word card with reading とき and audio as the plugin's 'the word wins' rule says; and make the book pass report a word it drops as a character repeat.
verdictReason: Every fact holds. Book, Lesson 4 Vocabulary > Time: 'とき 時 when . . . ; at the time of . . . (〜の)'. chapter-5/as-generated.json has r-2fdc2b012a91 時 'When; at the time of', ttsText とき; chapter-5/cards.json does not, and reading-report.json's 77 dropped entries name no 時. A grep of every cards.json in the collection finds 時 only in chapter-4 (r-2fdc2b012a91, 'Time', silent, pronunciation 'ji / toki', from the R&W 3 kanji table), so the word's meaning 'when' and its reading とき are on no card. Cause: the book pass's dropCharactersCardedEarlier (src/reading/characterGaps.js:237-250) removes any item whose target is a single kanji already carded as a character earlier, without checking that this one is a word, and logs the drop only to the console. Within one chapter the word wins over the character (card rule 4); across chapters nothing applies that rule, which is what this fix has to supply.

claim: Six word cards come only from grammar example sentences, exercise maps and a food picture, not from anything Lesson 4 presents as vocabulary, which card rule 1 excludes; the build's own coverage adversary flagged them as onlyInUnit.
evidence: 銀行 r-291477e39388 (Grammar 2 example 銀行は図書館のとなりです, Practice II-C map), 郵便局 r-6cc6046ae8ce (Practice II-A/C maps), 図書館 r-dbc8c3de0ea5 (Practice II heading and maps, Grammar 2 example), 大学 r-858bb23650b9 (Practice II maps, Let's Find Out), 高校 r-ef27a7ae8099 (Practice II-C map, VII-A prompt), 魚 r-32cac33e2772 (Practice III-C food picture label). None is in the Vocabulary, Location Words, Useful Expressions or Culture Notes lists. candidates/coverage.json onlyInUnit: [郵便局, 図書館, 先生, 銀行, 社長, 高校, 魚, 大学]. The words were taught in Lessons 1-2 in kana/romaji, so this is their first kanji appearance, not untaught vocabulary.
fix: Owner decision: either accept these as the first kanji spelling of words taught earlier in kana (and say so in card-rules-reading.md so the next chapter does the same), or exclude them with that reason, taking any kanji card that only they justify (銀, 郵, 便, 局, 図, 館) with them.
verdictReason: Checked each word against the chapter text: 銀行 appears only in Grammar 2's example (銀行は図書館のとなりです) and the Practice II-C maps; 郵便局 only in Practice II-A/C maps; 図書館 only in the Practice II heading, Grammar 2's example, the maps and the VII-C schedule; 大学 only in Grammar 3's example, Practice II-A and III-A, and Let's Find Out; 高校 only in the Practice II-C map and VII-A; 魚 only as a Practice III-C picture label. None is in the Vocabulary, Location Words, Useful Expressions, Culture Notes or Expression Notes lists, and candidates/coverage.json lists all six as onlyInUnit. card-rules-reading.md rule 1 puts a word that only appears in an exercise, an example sentence or a heading out, so as the rules stand these six cards are out, and with them the kanji cards 銀, 郵, 便, 局, 図, 館 (also 大 and 高) that no other word in this or an earlier unit uses. Rule 9's '銀行 and ぎんこう' example anticipates both spellings being carded but does not make an exercise appearance a teaching. Keeping them because they are the first kanji spelling of Lesson 1-2 words is a defensible owner exception, but it has to be written into card-rules-reading.md, as the Reader says; polish stays because the cards are correct in content.
